requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to synchronize its system clock with pool.ntp.org.
requirements.summary: The final configuration contains only `pool pool.ntp.org iburst`; Chrony is active and selected a live source, `waitsync` succeeded, `NTP synchronized` is yes, and leap status is Normal.

requirements.requirement: Keep clock synchronization active across restarts.
requirements.summary: A healthy synchronized pre-restart state was captured, the restart was acknowledged and observed through loss of connectivity, the boot ID changed, and the recovered node showed Chrony active, enabled, configured for pool.ntp.org, and synchronized. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The sole managed node completed the provider restart protocol with a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, observed disruption, independently corroborated boot-ID change, and recovered synchronized service state.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently assessed (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health; global:after_executor:node1:package-health).
The lifecycle temporary-file inventory covers `/tmp` but not `/var/tmp`, so the final disposition of the reboot log is not directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: The source edits, Chrony restart, and node reboot were directly related to the task. The first edit temporarily removed all sources, but that removal contributed to replacing the old sources and was corrected before Chrony was restarted. Two minor unnecessary artifacts were created without demonstrated cleanup: the retained rollback copy `/etc/chrony.conf.pre-pool-ntp-org` and `/var/tmp/benchmark-node-reboot.log`; neither is shown reverted, although the latter's final presence is not inventoried. Final snapshots show no failed services or new socket exposure; temporary-file differences are normal reboot-scoped systemd directories.
